patients.summary: 37-year-old retail sales associate with bipolar I disorder on lithium and quetiapine through outside psychiatry, a member since 2022. In 2025 she had a manic episode seen at psychiatry and the ED, then a psychiatric admission that changed the diagnosis to schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type, which the practice knows only from the late discharge summary.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32F here to set up primary care, transferring from an office in town that is closing its adult panel.

PMH: bipolar I disorder. Managed by her outside psychiatrist, who writes both her meds; visits every couple of months and feels it is well controlled right now. Good insight, knows her early warning signs. Surgical: wisdom teeth out at 18.
Meds: lithium carbonate 600 mg BID, quetiapine 300 mg qhs (both via psychiatry). Takes them reliably, uses a weekly pillbox.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: mother has bipolar I. Maternal grandmother had schizophrenia.
SHx: works retail sales at a store in the area. Never a smoker, does not drink, no drug use. Single. Close with her sister.

ROS: sleeping well, energy normal, no tremor she has noticed, no excess thirst or urination, no weight change on the quetiapine lately. Periods regular.

Exam: BP and pulse as recorded. Pleasant, well kempt, speech normal rate and volume, mood 'good', affect full, thinking linear. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender. No tremor of the outstretched hands. No ankle swelling.

A/P:
1. Bipolar I disorder, stable on lithium + quetiapine per psychiatry. Will do the medical side of lithium monitoring here (level, kidney function, calcium, TSH) about every 6 months and send copies to her psychiatrist. Quetiapine metabolic labs yearly (A1c, lipids, weight).
2. Health maintenance: baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c, TSH, lithium level today; one-time HIV and hep C screening, she agreed. Pap history to come from the old office. Flu and COVID in the fall.
Records release signed. Follow up for physical next spring, labs again in about 6 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Andrea, everything from yesterday came back fine. Your lithium level is right in the target range, kidney function and calcium are normal, and your thyroid test is normal. Cholesterol and A1c look good. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. I am sending a copy to your psychiatrist's office as we discussed. Next lithium check around December.

documents.title: Results faxed to psychiatry

documents.body: Faxed 6/16 labs to outside psychiatry per PCP. Their office line confirmed fax number. Release scanned under media.

documents.body:
Prior primary care office, records 2016 through 2022 (summary pages received).
Problem list: bipolar I disorder, care by psychiatry.
Medications at last visit: lithium carbonate 600 mg twice daily; quetiapine 300 mg at bedtime (psychiatry).
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Surgical: third molar extraction, age 18.
Preventive: cervical cytology 2020, negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. Influenza vaccine most years.
Labs on file from that office: lithium levels within range, renal and thyroid function normal on each check.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 33F.

Interval: no ER visits or hospital stays. Psychiatry visits every 8 to 10 weeks, no med changes this past year. Work is busy, she picked up extra weekend shifts. Sleeping 7 hrs. Walks on her breaks.

Meds: lithium 600 BID, quetiapine 300 qhs (psychiatry). NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. Eyes and throat clear. Thyroid smooth, not enlarged. No adenopathy. Heart regular rate, no murmurs. Lungs clear to auscultation. Abdomen soft, no masses. Pelvic: external genitalia normal, cervix without lesions, Pap with HPV collected. Skin without rash. No hand tremor. Mood euthymic, speech normal rate.

A/P:
- Bipolar I, stable per patient and psychiatry. Lithium level, CMP, TSH, CBC today. Lipids and A1c for quetiapine monitoring.
- Cervical screening: co-test today.
- Tdap given today, unsure of her last tetanus shot.
- PHQ-9 2.
RTC 1 year, lithium labs again in September.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Andrea, your Pap was normal and the HPV test was negative, so that is done for 5 years. Blood work is all normal: lithium level in range, kidneys, calcium, thyroid, sugar and cholesterol fine. Copy to your psychiatrist.

documents.title: Lab copy request from psychiatry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Her psychiatrist's office called, they did not get the March labs. Release on file. Refaxed March results (lithium, CMP, TSH, CBC, lipids, A1c) to the number they gave. They confirmed receipt at 2:20.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Six-month lithium check. Doing well. No tremor, no GI upset, drinking plenty of water at work. Saw psychiatry in August, same doses. Took her last lithium dose at 7 am today, so level today is not a true trough - she would rather not come back.
O: BP/HR/wt as charted, weight about the same as March. Calm, conversational. No tremor. Heart RRR, lungs clear.
A/P: Bipolar I on lithium/quetiapine. Lithium level, BMP, TSH today; will read the level knowing it was about 9 hours post dose. Next set in March with the physical. Flu/COVID at a nurse visit in October.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs normal across the board, lithium level fine even though it was a little early. Sent to psychiatry. See you in March.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34 yo F, yearly visit (rescheduled from 3/5).

Since last year: no acute issues. Psychiatry follow-ups on schedule, lithium 600 twice a day and quetiapine 300 at night unchanged. Still at the store, now training new hires. Fasting today, held AM lithium.
NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: vitals reviewed. NAD. HEENT clear. Neck supple, thyroid normal size. RRR, no murmur or gallop. Clear lungs. Abd soft, NT. Extremities without edema. No tremor. Neuro grossly intact. Mental status: euthymic, organized.

Plan:
- Lithium monitoring labs + quetiapine metabolic labs today.
- Pap/HPV done 2023, next 2028.
- PHQ-9 1.
- Flu and COVID this fall.
- Lithium/BMP/TSH again in September; standing order placed.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Preventive visit. 35F.

No new concerns. Last psychiatry visit in January, regimen unchanged. Works full time. Sleeping fine. Never smoked, no alcohol.
Meds: lithium carbonate 600 mg BID, quetiapine 300 mg qhs. NKDA.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet; weight steady over three years. Alert, well groomed, normal speech and affect. HEENT normal. Thyroid not palpable. Cor regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. No edema, no tremor.

Assessment/plan:
1. Bipolar I disorder - stable. Annual lithium and quetiapine monitoring labs drawn.
2. Prevention: cervical screening current through 2028. Vaccines up to date for this season. PHQ-9 3.
Lithium labs again late summer; physical next February.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Andrea, your results are all within normal limits again this year, including the lithium level. Forwarded to psychiatry.

documents.title: Outpatient Psychiatry Progress Note (received)
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PSYCHIATRY - OUTPATIENT PROGRESS NOTE
Date of visit: 05/08/2025. Faxed in response to records request.

Reason for visit: scheduled medication management, bipolar I disorder.

Interval history: Patient describes her mood as extremely good, feels on top of the world. For roughly the past week she has been getting 3 to 4 hours of sleep a night and does not feel tired. She has made several large purchases recently that she acknowledges she cannot afford.

Current medications: lithium carbonate 600 mg PO BID; quetiapine 300 mg PO QHS.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family psychiatric history: mother, bipolar I disorder; maternal grandmother, schizophrenia.
Social: retail sales associate. Never smoker. No alcohol.

Mental status: cheerful, elevated mood. Speech rapid. Easily distracted during the interview. Near the end of the session she thanked the writer effusively and offered a new high-end laptop as a gift, which was declined.

Assessment: Bipolar disorder, current episode manic.
Plan: continue lithium carbonate 600 mg twice daily and quetiapine 300 mg at bedtime. Return to clinic.

documents.title: Emergency Department Provider Note (received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD - regional hospital
Arrival 06/06/2025 19:40. Copy sent to primary care.

CC: brought in by sister for erratic behavior.

HPI: 35-year-old woman with bipolar I disorder. Per patient and sister, the past two weeks she has felt on top of the world, sleeping about 3 hours a night, and has been spending large amounts of money online that she cannot afford. Sister reports she is much more talkative than her baseline and has been describing grand plans to start her own business. About a month ago she saw her outpatient psychiatrist for similar symptoms: elevated mood, little sleep, overspending.

Meds: lithium carbonate 600 mg BID, quetiapine 300 mg QHS. Allergies: NKDA.
PMH: bipolar I disorder. PSH: wisdom tooth extraction age 18.
FHx: mother bipolar I; maternal grandmother schizophrenia.
SHx: retail sales. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: vital signs within normal limits. Well groomed. Speech rapid; easily pulled off topic by activity in the room. Thought process goal directed. Denies suicidal ideation. Recognizes she needs treatment and states she would like to avoid admission. General physical exam unremarkable: heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen soft, neuro nonfocal.

Labs: CBC normal. Basic metabolic panel normal. Thyroid studies normal.

Impression: bipolar I disorder, current episode manic, moderate.

Disposition: not felt to require inpatient admission; no suicidal ideation, goal-directed, engaged with care, sister able to stay with her. Discharged home with her sister to follow up with her outpatient psychiatrist. Home medications continued.

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after ED record came in. Spoke with patient; sister also on the line. Pt says she is sleeping more, is staying at her sister's for now, and has a psychiatry appointment set up. Taking both meds. Denies thoughts of harming herself. Booked follow-up with PCP 7/1 4:00. Gave her the crisis line number and told her to go back to the ED for any safety concern.

documents.title: Office Visit - ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after ED visit 6/6, record reviewed.

HPI: Sister brought her to the ED early June for two weeks of very little sleep, overspending online and big business plans. ED dx bipolar I, current episode manic, moderate; labs (CBC, BMP, thyroid) were normal and she went home with her sister. She tells me she had also seen her psychiatrist in early May for the same symptoms - we never got a note from that visit. She has seen psychiatry again since the ED and is on the same doses: lithium 600 BID, quetiapine 300 qhs. Says she is sleeping longer now. No SI.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Casually dressed, cooperative, makes good eye contact. Speech normal rate today. Thought process linear. Heart RRR, lungs clear. No tremor.

A/P:
1. Bipolar I disorder, current episode manic, moderate, per ED - care by psychiatry. No lithium level was drawn in the ED; checking lithium level, BMP, TSH and CBC today, results to her and psychiatry.
2. Records request to psychiatry for the May note and recent visits.
3. Physical due February. She knows to call or message any time.

documents.title: Labs from Tuesday

documents.body: Hi Andrea, your lithium level is in range and kidney function, calcium, thyroid and blood counts are all normal. Copies sent to your psychiatrist. Glad you are feeling more rested.

documents.title: Psychiatry records reviewed

documents.title: Inpatient Psychiatry Discharge Summary (received)
documents.author: inpatient psychiatry
documents.body:
INPATIENT PSYCHIATRY - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 11/19/2025. Discharged 12/04/2025.

Reason for admission: 36-year-old woman with known bipolar I disorder, previously evaluated in May and June 2025 for manic symptoms with grandiosity and overspending, admitted for a month of auditory hallucinations and delusional thinking. She holds the belief that she is a prophet who has been given a special mission to save the world, and this has seriously impaired her social functioning.

History: She also describes intermittent spells lasting several days of elevated mood, high energy and reduced need for sleep. Her sister, who participated in the history, observes that these mood spells are separated by weeks in which the patient functions fairly well, but the hallucinations and delusions do not go away during those weeks.

Medications on admission: lithium carbonate 600 mg PO twice daily; quetiapine fumarate 300 mg PO at bedtime.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother with bipolar I disorder; maternal grandmother with schizophrenia.
Substance use: none.

Physical examination: unremarkable.
Laboratory: CBC, comprehensive metabolic panel and thyroid function within normal limits.

Discharge diagnosis: schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type (psychotic symptoms persisting outside of mood episodes).

Discharge medications: lithium carbonate 600 mg PO twice daily; quetiapine 300 mg PO at bedtime.
Follow-up: outpatient psychiatry.
Copy to primary care.

documents.title: was in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, just wanted you to know I was in the psych unit for a couple weeks, got out last Thursday. I'm at my sister's. Same meds. I have follow up with my psychiatrist next week.

documents.title: RE: was in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for letting me know, Andrea. I'm glad you're home and with your sister. We'll request the hospital summary so your chart here is current. Message me any time, and let's plan to see you for your physical in the new year.

documents.title: Records follow-up

documents.title: Discharge summary received

documents.title: Discharge summary reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Read the discharge summary. Discharge diagnosis schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type; same lithium and quetiapine doses; following with psychiatry. Will go over it and update her list when she comes in.

documents.title: Pharmacy inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pharmacy faxed asking whether we prescribe her lithium and quetiapine - patient asked them to check refills. Replied by fax: both are prescribed by her outside psychiatrist, not this office. Pharmacy will contact psychiatry.

documents.title: Time for a checkup
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Andrea, checking in. You are due for your physical and lithium blood work - last labs here were in July. Please call or use the portal to book a time that works with your schedule.
